source.title: Training Two-Layer ReLU Networks with Gradient Descent is Inconsistent

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent cutoff or corruption.
record.tranche_reason: The paper's own theory and experiments show that gradient descent can fail to learn useful nonlinear predictors under particular two-layer-network and initialization conditions. Its measures and settings do not directly test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. (2017) and Safran and Shamir (2018), but those cited results are not this paper's evidence. Its own experiments report kink-crossing probabilities and synthetic-data RMSE, not CIFAR classification training error, teacher-student spurious-minimum rates, or the other listed version measures.
record.test_reason: The study establishes optimization failures in shallow regression networks, but none of V1–V6 is tested. Its width experiments do not use V2's teacher–student setting or extra-student-neuron comparison; its initialization experiments do not measure V4's propagation, training-speed or trainable-depth outcomes.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. More precisely, the authors prove high-probability optimization failure for certain fixed data sets even with overparameterization, and statistical inconsistency for specified sampled distributions in an underparameterized regime. Their synthetic experiments show related failures beyond the theorem's assumptions and improvements from alternative initializations, parameterizations and optimizers, without establishing universal consistency for those alternatives.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes two-layer (Leaky)ReLU networks trained by GD on least-squares loss, mainly on constructed regression distributions. It does not use the listed benchmark classification recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with optimizer, early stopping, step size, input dimension, bias initialization, parameterization, and optimizer choice.

fits_no_version.finding: With zero biases and He initialization, kink-crossing probabilities decrease with width on the constructed one- and two-dimensional distributions. Early stopping further reduces crossings; crossing a sample does not necessarily improve MSE beyond the arm-wise affine baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For some synthetic regression distributions, wider shallow ReLU networks trained with gradient methods increasingly remain confined to predictors determined by their initial activation regions.

fits_no_version.finding: Example 1 admits zero empirical risk with at least six hidden neurons, yet sufficiently small-step GD has empirical risk at least 1 with high probability under the stated initialization; the failure probability approaches one as width grows.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Arbitrary overparameterization need not eliminate optimization failure for specially constructed shallow ReLU regression problems with zero-bias initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 10 and Table L.1 show synthetic test-RMSE differences across bias initializations, parameterizations and optimizers, especially in low input dimensions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Bias initialization and parameterization can materially affect shallow ReLU regression performance on targets with nonlinear radial dependence.

record.problems: The central theory applies to specific one-dimensional distributions, zero-bias initialization, and step-size constraints. Experiments use synthetic data; several relevant plots report Monte-Carlo estimates without numeric values in the text. Section 10 primarily reports test RMSE, not training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: Section 10 and Table L.1 report many synthetic-data test-RMSE comparisons across initialization, optimizer, parameterization, and input dimension. They are not rows for a listed version because they do not measure its named training-error, propagation, depth, stability, or normalization outcomes; their qualitative findings are summarized in fits_no_version.

untested.parts: CIFAR convolutional-network training classification error, including random labels and size, stopping and regularization comparisons.
Realizable ReLU teacher–student problems, joint teacher/student growth and adding one or two student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation, identity shortcuts and the specified deep-network alternatives.
Activation-matched signal and gradient propagation, learning-speed comparisons and maximum trainable depth, including orthogonal initialization.
Recovery, divergence and sharpness dynamics around learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including the Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's tests/T5 assignment is inconsistent with its correctly unlinked rows. These results address neighboring optimization claims, rather than contradicting any version as stated. No listed-version result requires an additional row.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training classification error, corrupted or random labels, and the stated size, stopping, and regularization comparisons.
Teacher-student experiments varying teacher and student widths and measuring spurious-minimum frequency.
Depth sweeps comparing plain and residual networks, and the cited special deep-network recipes.
Signal and gradient propagation, training speed, and maximum trainable depth under the specified initializations.
Training-loss and sharpness dynamics as learning rates cross stability thresholds.
Batch-normalization comparisons for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network (He initialization)
rows.operation_detail: GD or SGD training; estimate probability that a kink leaves (−1, 1)
rows.measure: Probability of a kink crossing a sample during training
rows.note: The text says probabilities decrease with increasing width and that early stopping can reduce kink crossings; exact plotted values are not stated. This is a proxy for the paper's training-failure analysis, not a listed version's measure.
rows.check: Figure 5 combines GD and SGD, with and without early stopping, and different step sizes; these should be separate condition rows. The optimizer condition incorrectly lists only GD. The measured event is a kink leaving the gap around zero, rather than a direct measurement of any claim version. Exact probabilities cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network (He initialization)
rows.operation_detail: GD training; estimate kink-crossing probability and probability MSE passes a stated threshold

conditions.value: uniform distribution on the 33-point dataset from Figure 7

rows.measure: Probabilities of kink crossing a sample and MSE falling below 0.999999 times the best affine MSE
rows.note: The text states that kink-crossing probability decreases with width and that MSE often does not pass the threshold even when a kink reaches a data point. Exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: Separate kink-crossing probability from MSE-threshold probability. The threshold is 0.999999 times the best MSE for functions affine separately on each of the 11 radial arms, rather than the best globally affine MSE. Exact probabilities cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
